summary: Almost all of your views come from Instagram, not YouTube. The PIR motion sensor video is the clear winner, with about 1,400 Instagram views and the most likes, shares and saves, and the other Hindi 'how does this everyday thing work' videos do modestly on Instagram. YouTube is barely moving (most videos under 80 views), and the only English video got a little YouTube reach and nothing on Instagram. Newer videos are also still early, so their numbers may grow.
winningPattern: Hindi explainer about a sensor people meet in daily life (motion, street light, phone, door), posted on Instagram. The title opens with a curiosity question or a surprising claim ('Aapko Dekhta Nahi!', 'Ungli Nahi, Bijli!'), uses simple Hinglish, and ends with 🤔 #shorts. The best one pairs a bold 'it doesn't work how you think' statement with a familiar object.
doMore: Lead with a surprising myth-busting claim in the title, like the PIR 'doesn't see you' hook
Pick everyday objects people touch or walk past daily (sensors in homes, malls, phones, streets)
Keep narration in Hindi/Hinglish, since every Hindi video reached Instagram and the English one did not
Prioritise Instagram, and end each video with a share or save prompt like 'dost ko bhejo' since shares and saves signal quality
Repost your top-performing topic from a new angle (e.g. PIR in lights, alarms, taps) to build on what worked
stopDoing: Publishing English-only videos for now, as they got no Instagram traction
Niche or abstract topics with no visible daily-life link (heartbeat via light, ultrasonic) without a stronger hook
Posting several videos in a few days with weak hooks; spend the effort on a sharper first line instead
